name: Motivation
description: Simple, evidence-informed ways to start and keep going: specific plans, small next steps, tracking, and a kind response to setbacks.

steps.text: Pick one goal and name the very next small step.
Make an if-then plan: when and where you will do that step.
Note each time you do it, so progress is visible.
After a missed day, treat it as information and plan the next step, without blame.

claims.text: A specific if-then plan for when and where to act can make follow-through more likely.
Tracking progress can support reaching a goal.
Breaking a goal into small next steps may make starting easier.
Responding to a setback with self-compassion may help people get back on track.

safety_notes: Not medical advice. Persistent low mood or loss of interest is a reason to speak to a clinician.
Never use shame or guilt as a motivator.
Crisis language is handled by the fixed referral response before any model call.
